summary: Researched the public 'pstack skills' project, identifying it as Lauren Tan's Cursor plugin for rigorous AI-assisted engineering (source: cursor/plugins repo, MIT, version 0.14.3). Scraped the plugin manifest, README, setup/poteto-mode/automate-me/create-verification-skill SKILL.md files, the docs guide, and Cursor's official Skills and Plugins documentation to summarize its UX patterns (router skills, sticky modes, playbooks-as-todos, role-based model routing, project-local verification) and file conventions (per-skill directory with required SKILL.md, optional scripts/references/assets, plugin.json manifest declaring skills/agents roots). Produced a report of concise product inspiration for an AI skills manager, including interoperability caveats between pstack's host-specific frontmatter and the open Agent Skills specification. No files were edited.
decisions: Treat cursor/plugins as the canonical source for pstack and other repositories (e.g., backnotprop/pstack) as mirrors.
Flag that pstack frontmatter (e.g., 'Poteto Mode') may diverge from the portable Agent Skills specification, which requires lowercase hyphenated names matching the directory.
Position pstack as a skill collection and workflow router, not a standalone skills manager.
